summaries.summary: Economics is the social science concerned with the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. The American Economic Association, a scholarly society in the field, describes economics on its student resources as "a broad discipline that helps us understand historical trends, interpret today's headlines, and make predictions about the coming years," noting that its study "ranges from the very small to the very large"—from microeconomics, "the study of individual decisions," to macroeconomics, "the study of the economy as a whole." The Association describes itself as "a nonprofit, nonpartisan, scholarly association with more than 17,000 members from academia, government, and business who are committed to the advancement of economics and its enduring contributions to society." In the Library of Congress Classification, economic theory falls within class HB, whose authority record bears the caption "Economic theory. Demography."

summaries.summary: Sociology is the social science that studies human society and social behavior. The American Sociological Association, on its "What Is Sociology?" resource, defines it as "the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior," explaining that "Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies and how people interact within these contexts," so that "the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to global communities." The Association describes itself as having been "founded in 1905" and as "the national professional membership association for sociologists and others who are interested in sociology," with a mission to "advance sociology as a science and profession, and promote the contributions and use of sociology to society." In the Library of Congress Classification the discipline occupies class HM, whose authority record carries the caption "Sociology."

summaries.summary: Political science is the social science concerned with the study of government, politics, and power. Encyclopaedia Britannica describes it as "the systematic study of governance by the application of empirical and generally scientific methods of analysis," adding that "As traditionally defined and studied, political science examines the state and its organs and institutions." The American Political Science Association, founded in 1903, describes itself as bringing "together political scientists from all fields of inquiry, regions, and occupational endeavors within and outside academe to deepen our understanding of politics, democracy, and citizenship throughout the world." In the Library of Congress Classification the discipline's general works fall within class JA, whose authority record carries the caption "Political science (General)."

summaries.summary: As an academic field, education is the scholarly discipline that studies teaching, learning, and the conditions under which they occur. Encyclopaedia Britannica describes education as "a discipline that is concerned with methods of teaching and learning in schools or school-like environments as opposed to various nonformal and informal means of socialization." The American Educational Research Association, a research society founded in 1916, describes itself as "a national research society" that "strives to advance knowledge about education, to encourage scholarly inquiry related to education, and to promote the use of research to improve education and serve the public good," and as "concerned with improving the educational process by encouraging scholarly inquiry related to education and evaluation." In the Library of Congress Classification, general works on education fall within class L, whose authority record carries the caption "Education (General)," with the theory and practice of education classed in LB.

summaries.summary: As an academic discipline, law is the field of scholarship concerned with legal rules, institutions, and reasoning. Encyclopaedia Britannica describes law as "the discipline and profession concerned with the customs, practices, and rules of conduct of a community that are recognized as binding by the community," noting that "Enforcement of the body of rules is through a controlling authority." The Association of American Law Schools, which describes itself as "a 501(c)(3) nonprofit association" of member law schools, states that it was "Founded in 1900" and that its mission "is to improve and advance legal education," pursued "by promoting the core values of excellence in teaching and scholarship, academic freedom, and diversity of viewpoints." In the Library of Congress Classification the discipline occupies class K, whose general authority record carries the caption "Law in general. Comparative and uniform law. Jurisprudence."

summaries.summary: Anthropology is the social science that studies human beings, their societies, and their development. The American Anthropological Association, on its "What Is Anthropology?" resource, describes anthropology as "the study of what makes us human," explaining that to grasp "the full sweep and complexity of cultures across all of human history, anthropology draws and builds upon knowledge from the social and biological sciences as well as the humanities and physical sciences." The Association notes that "In the community of anthropologists in the United States, these four fields—human biology, archaeology, cultural anthropology, and linguistics—are understood to be the pillars on which the whole discipline rests," while observing that any individual anthropologist "will probably specialize in one or two of these areas but have general familiarity with them all." In the Library of Congress Classification the discipline occupies class GN, whose authority record carries the caption "Anthropology."
